issue.title: Archive waiting.json for runners dead longer than N hours after deciding TUI, retention, and lifecycle effects

task_type_fields.proposal:
Add a housekeeping sweep that archives (renames or moves) `waiting.json` for runners that have been provably dead for longer than N hours. At sase-1hf.4 measurement time, 795 of 904 markers on athena belonged to dead runners. Most are older than 7 days.

First decide the effect on every consumer that treats `waiting.json` as a live marker:
- TUI `WAITING` status (`src/sase/ace/tui/models/_loaders/_meta_enrichment_filesystem.py`)
- continuation retention (`src/sase/core/continuation_retention.py`)
- project lifecycle live markers (`src/sase/main/project_handler_lifecycle.py`)
- the runner-slot queue and the artifact index waiting projection

Reuse `sase.axe.wait_marker_scan.scan_waiting_markers` plus `waiting_runner_liveness` (dead = `stopped_at` or a recorded pid that `is_process_alive` reports gone). Never archive `unknown` liveness.

Proposed by phase bead sase-1hf.5 (lane-split) in PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1, item 4. Also the deferred third item of task sase-1hd. Filed by the sase-1hf land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: sase-1hf deliberately deferred this. Its live-waiter filter already makes dead markers cost `wait_checks` ~0.04 s, so the sweep is hygiene, not latency. Removing or renaming the marker also changes TUI, retention, and lifecycle behaviour, which needs its own decision.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1hf skips dead waiters but leaves ~800 dead waiting.json markers in place because removing them changes live-marker semantics elsewhere; that decision and sweep need their own task.
